items.prompt: Explore the application and discover user journeys.

proposed.name: Navigate core blockchain dashboard sections (Chain, Wallets, Mining) and verify each renders
proposed.description: Exercise the app's primary blockchain UI by navigating from the dashboard through the three core CHAIN-section tabs — Chain, Wallets, and Mining — verifying that each section switch produces meaningful blockchain-related content (block list, wallet list, mining status) rather than a blank or broken page. This corresponds to the design doc's requirement that the dashboard at / shows the blockchain UI and that chain, wallet, and mining endpoints are exercised.

proposed.name: Memorize a text and reconstruct + sign a block — the core blockchain mining workflow
proposed.description: The dashboard's primary workflow (explicitly prompted by 'Aucun bloc miné — mémorisez un graphe puis signez') is to memorize a text via the Quick start 'Memorize a text' → Go action, then reconstruct and sign a block via the 'Reconstruct + sign block' → Go action. This journey exercises that end-to-end flow — the app's core IR-learn and block-signing functionality corresponding to /api/v1/ir/learn and the chain/block-creation endpoints — and verifies that each step produces meaningful content (an IR learning form/confirmation and a block reconstruction/signing result) rather than a blank or broken page.

proposed.name: View P2P network peers, system logs, and debug console — blockchain infrastructure monitoring
proposed.description: Navigate from the dashboard through the SYSTEM-section tabs — P2P Network (S14), Logs (S11), and Console (S12) — verifying that each section renders meaningful blockchain infrastructure content: a peer list / network status view (corresponding to /api/v1/p2p/status and /api/v1/p2p/peers), live demo logs (corresponding to /api/v1/dashboard/logs/demo-live), and an interactive debug console. This exercises the core infrastructure monitoring surfaces of the ARTCB blockchain dashboard that no existing journey covers.

proposed.name: Create a new wallet and verify it appears in the wallet list — the blockchain wallet generation flow
proposed.description: Navigate to the Wallets section and exercise the wallet creation form — fill the wallet name field and click Generate — then verify the new wallet appears in the wallet list and can be selected. This covers the design doc's /api/v1/wallet/create and /api/v1/wallet/list functionality, a core blockchain surface no existing journey exercises. The wallet creation form fields (S33 name input and S34 Generate button) are the primary wallet management workflow of the ARTCB dashboard.

This corresponds to the design doc's requirement that the dashboard at / shows the blockchain UI and that chain, wallet, and mining endpoints are exercised.

proposed.name: View Governance PoL scores, API Keys, and AI Memory — blockchain governance and access management sections
proposed.description: Navigate from the dashboard through three untouched CORE/SYSTEM sections — Governance (S15, corresponding to /api/v1/pol/score Proof-of-Learn scoring), API Keys (S17, for blockchain API access management), and AI Memory (S18) — verifying that each section switch renders meaningful governance/access/memory content rather than a blank or broken page. These are core ARTCB dashboard surfaces that no existing journey exercises.

proposed.name: Fill the Memorize IR-learning form end-to-end — session, LLM toggle, distributed calc toggle, source text, and submit
proposed.description: Navigate to the Memorize page and fully exercise the IR-learning data-entry form: fill the session_id field, toggle the use_llm checkbox, toggle the distributed calculation (pool E2E) checkbox, load a sample source via the Charger Wailly button (or type source text), then click Memorize to submit. Verify that the form submits and the Proof-of-Learning / graph-building panel shows progress or a result rather than staying idle. This covers the design doc's /api/v1/ir/learn endpoint — the core IR learning workflow — with every form field exercised, which no existing journey does (journey 2 only describes the combined quick-start navigation, not the full form). The form fields (S26 session, S27 use_llm, S28 distributed calc, S30 source text, S31 Memorize, S32 Charger Wailly) are all now visible and testable.

This exercises the core infrastructure monitoring surfaces of the ARTCB blockchain dashboard that no existing journey covers.

proposed.name: Configure an AI provider integration end-to-end — select provider, fill name, model, and API key, then connect
proposed.description: Navigate to the Integrations section (S13) and fully exercise the AI provider configuration form: select a provider from the dropdown (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, or OpenRouter), fill the integration name field, fill the model field, fill the API key field, then click Connect. Verify that the form submits and produces a connection confirmation or status change rather than staying idle. This covers the ARTCB dashboard's AI integration configuration — a core surface that feeds the IR-learning and Proof-of-Learning workflows — with every form field exercised. No existing journey covers the Integrations page or its configuration form (S41–S45).

proposed.name: Create a blockchain group and join it — the group formation and wallet-binding workflow
proposed.description: Navigate to the Groups section (S16) and fully exercise the group creation form: fill the group name field, fill any configuration fields (version, etc.), select an active wallet, click Create, then click Join to join the group. Verify that the group is created and that joining produces a confirmation or membership status change. This covers the ARTCB dashboard's group governance workflow — a core blockchain community/consensus surface with a multi-field form (S53–S60) that no existing journey exercises. It corresponds to the design doc's requirement that all blockchain core surfaces be tested.

proposed.name: Add a P2P network peer and synchronize all peers — blockchain network management workflow
proposed.description: Navigate to the P2P Network section (S14) and exercise the peer management workflow: fill the peer connection detail fields (S47, S48, S49 — fields with no visible label or placeholder identifying them, so the user cannot tell what each box expects), click Ajouter (S50) to add the peer, then click Synchroniser tous les pairs (S46) to sync the full peer list. Verify that adding a peer produces feedback (a confirmation or the peer appearing in the list) and that synchronization produces a status update or confirmation. This exercises the design doc's /api/v1/p2p/peers endpoint functionality beyond mere viewing — the core blockchain networking peer-addition and sync workflow that no existing journey covers (journey 3 only navigates to P2P/Logs/Console without exercising the peer form).

proposed.description: Navigate to the Console section (S12) and exercise the interactive CLI console: type a 'help' command into the command input field (S39), click Execute (S40), and verify that the console returns a meaningful response — a help listing, command output, or API reference — rather than staying empty or producing an error. This covers the ARTCB dashboard's debug console interactive functionality — the 'terminal equivalent' for the full API that the design doc describes — which journey 3 only navigates to without exercising. The console is a primary developer-facing surface of the blockchain API and its command execution behavior is completely untested.

This covers the design doc's /api/v1/wallet/create and /api/v1/wallet/list functionality, a core blockchain surface no existing journey exercises. The wallet creation form fields (S33 name input and S34 Generate button) are the primary wallet management workflow of the ARTCB dashboard.

existingJourneys.name: Fill the Memorize IR-learning form end-to-end — session, LLM toggle, distributed calc toggle, source text, and submit
existingJourneys.description: Navigate to the Memorize page and fully exercise the IR-learning data-entry form: fill the session_id field, toggle the use_llm checkbox, toggle the distributed calculation (pool E2E) checkbox, load a sample source via the Charger Wailly button (or type source text), then click Memorize to submit. Verify that the form submits and the Proof-of-Learning / graph-building panel shows progress or a result rather than staying idle. This covers the design doc's /api/v1/ir/learn endpoint — the core IR learning workflow — with every form field exercised, which no existing journey does (journey 2 only describes the combined quick-start navigation, not the full form). The form fields (S26 session, S27 use_llm, S28 distributed calc, S30 source text, S31 Memorize, S32 Charger Wailly) are all now visible and testable.

existingJourneys.name: Configure an AI provider integration end-to-end — select provider, fill name, model, and API key, then connect
existingJourneys.description: Navigate to the Integrations section (S13) and fully exercise the AI provider configuration form: select a provider from the dropdown (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, or OpenRouter), fill the integration name field, fill the model field, fill the API key field, then click Connect. Verify that the form submits and produces a connection confirmation or status change rather than staying idle. This covers the ARTCB dashboard's AI integration configuration — a core surface that feeds the IR-learning and Proof-of-Learning workflows — with every form field exercised. No existing journey covers the Integrations page or its configuration form (S41–S45).

existingJourneys.name: Create a blockchain group and join it — the group formation and wallet-binding workflow
existingJourneys.description: Navigate to the Groups section (S16) and fully exercise the group creation form: fill the group name field, fill any configuration fields (version, etc.), select an active wallet, click Create, then click Join to join the group. Verify that the group is created and that joining produces a confirmation or membership status change. This covers the ARTCB dashboard's group governance workflow — a core blockchain community/consensus surface with a multi-field form (S53–S60) that no existing journey exercises. It corresponds to the design doc's requirement that all blockchain core surfaces be tested.

existingJourneys.name: Add a P2P network peer and synchronize all peers — blockchain network management workflow
existingJourneys.description: Navigate to the P2P Network section (S14) and exercise the peer management workflow: fill the peer connection detail fields (S47, S48, S49 — fields with no visible label or placeholder identifying them, so the user cannot tell what each box expects), click Ajouter (S50) to add the peer, then click Synchroniser tous les pairs (S46) to sync the full peer list. Verify that adding a peer produces feedback (a confirmation or the peer appearing in the list) and that synchronization produces a status update or confirmation. This exercises the design doc's /api/v1/p2p/peers endpoint functionality beyond mere viewing — the core blockchain networking peer-addition and sync workflow that no existing journey covers (journey 3 only navigates to P2P/Logs/Console without exercising the peer form).

existingJourneys.name: Generate an API key end-to-end — fill the key name, set expiry, and generate — verifying the key is created with a confirmation
Fill the AI Memory form and create a memory entry — the AI contributor registration workflow
existingJourneys.description: Navigate to the AI Memory section (S18) and fully exercise the AI memory creation form: fill the contributor/agent name field (S61, placeholder 'Cursor dev, ChatGPT bot, LangChain…') and activate the submit control (S62). Verify that the form submits and produces a confirmation or that the new memory entry appears in the list rather than staying idle. Journey 5 only navigates to the AI Memory page without exercising its form — this journey covers the data-entry form the AI Memory page exposes, satisfying the form-coverage requirement for a page whose primary purpose is to register AI agents/contributors that feed the Proof-of-Learning and IR-learning workflows.

existingJourneys.name: Create a governance proposal — select voting wallet, fill title/description/version, and submit
existingJourneys.description: Navigate to the Governance section and fully exercise the governance proposal creation form: select a voting wallet (S52), fill the title field (S53, which has no visible label or placeholder identifying it, so the user cannot tell what the box expects), fill the description field (S54, also unlabeled/unplaceholdered), fill the version field (S55), then click Créer (S56) to submit the proposal. Verify that the proposal is created and the app gives feedback — a confirmation, the new proposal appearing in the Propositions list, or a status change — rather than nothing happening. This covers the ARTCB dashboard's on-chain governance workflow (1 wallet = 1 vote, community accepts/rejects major updates), a core blockchain consensus surface whose data-entry form no existing journey exercises. Journey 5 only navigates to the Governance page without filling the form; journey 8 covers the Groups page, not Governance proposals. The title and description fields present no visible label or placeholder, so a user cannot recognize what each box expects from the field itself — a recognition defect this journey exposes.

existingJourneys.name: Create an AI Memory memo and engrave it in the blockchain — the AI-observation-to-on-chain-commit workflow
existingJourneys.description: Navigate to the AI Memory section and exercise the full memo creation pipeline: click New memo, select a memo type (observation/bugfix/lesson/decision/hypothesis/goal/proof), fill the label field, click + Ajouter to add the memo, then click 'Graver dans la blockchain' to commit the memo on-chain. Verify that the memo is created with feedback and that the engrave action produces a confirmation or on-chain commit status. This covers the core ARTCB Proof-of-Learning workflow where AI agent observations and decisions are recorded as memos and then committed to the blockchain — a primary function of the AI Memory section (S70, S84, S77, S78, S86) that no existing journey exercises. Journey 12 only fills the AI contributor registration form; this journey covers the memo creation and blockchain engraving workflow, which is the section's primary on-chain functionality.

proposed.name: Add an AI Memory webhook endpoint — fill URL and label, submit, and verify the webhook is registered
proposed.description: Navigate to the AI Memory section, click the Webhooks tab (S73), and fully exercise the webhook creation form that was revealed: fill the webhook URL field (S76, placeholder 'URL HTTPS (https://...)') and the label field (S77, placeholder 'Label'), then click '+ Ajouter' (S78) to submit. Verify that adding the webhook produces feedback — a confirmation message, the new webhook appearing in an active webhooks list, or a status change — rather than nothing happening. Journey 17 navigates to the Webhooks tab and describes viewing webhook management content, but the actual webhook creation form (S76–S78) has never been filled and submitted. This is a data-entry form whose primary purpose is to register an HTTPS endpoint that external AI tools (Cursor, ChatGPT, LangChain) receive live blockchain memory updates at — a core integration surface of the ARTCB AI Memory backend. The form-coverage rule requires exercising it rather than leaving it as a visited-but-unfilled page.

This journey changes the visibility from the default private to public, navigates to the P2P Network section to verify the setting is reflected in the network status, then clicks 'Synchroniser tous les pairs' (S46) and verifies the sync responds with a status update under the new visibility mode. This chains the visibility change with a P2P synchronization to form a complete network-configuration workflow rather than a single dropdown toggle, and it corresponds to the design doc's /api/v1/chain/status and /api/v1/p2p/status endpoints whose visibility field is never tested by any existing journey.

It verifies that the engrave action produces explicit success-or-failure feedback (a confirmation, a block commit status, or an on-chain transaction record) rather than silently doing nothing — a commit control that changes nothing observable is a Visibility-of-System-Status defect. This is the core Proof-of-Learning on-chain commit: AI agent observations are recorded as memos and committed to the blockchain, which is the primary function of the AI Memory section.

existingJourneys.name: Connect an existing wallet by address — the wallet access/login flow

existingJourneys.name: Add an AI Memory webhook endpoint — fill URL and label, submit, and verify the webhook is registered

existingJourneys.name: Configure AI Memory webhooks and open a live data stream — the external AI tool real-time integration pipeline

This journey changes the visibility from the default private to public, navigates to the P2P Network section to verify the setting is reflected in the network status, then clicks 'Synchroniser tous les pairs' (S46) and verifies the sync responds with a status update under the new visibility mode. This chains the visibility change with a P2P synchronization to form a complete network-configuration workflow rather than a single dropdown toggle, and it corresponds to the design doc's /api/v1/chain/status and /api/v1/p2p/status endpoints whose visibility field is never tested by any existing journey.

existingJourneys.name: Switch the dashboard UI language and verify the interface updates — the localization configuration workflow
existingJourneys.description: The dashboard header exposes a language selector with seven options (FR, EN, ZH, ES, PT, IT, RU — S87–S93) that switches the entire ARTCB dashboard UI between languages. No existing journey exercises this. This journey clicks the EN button (S88) to switch from the default French to English, verifies that the navigation labels, section headings, and dashboard widgets update to English text rather than staying in French, then clicks another language (e.g. ZH via S89) and verifies the UI changes again. This is a complete user-preference configuration workflow — the user changes their display language and confirms the interface responds — and it exercises the internationalization system that is a core UI feature of the dashboard. A dead language button that changes nothing on the page fails the abstract verification checks.

existingJourneys.name: Reconstruct and sign a blockchain block via the Quick Start action — the core block-commit workflow
existingJourneys.description: The dashboard's Quick Start section lists 'Reconstruct + sign block' with a → Go action (S22) — the second half of the core mining workflow that the dashboard prompt 'Aucun bloc miné — mémorisez un graphe puis signez' explicitly directs the user to perform after memorizing text. No existing journey navigates to this page or exercises the block reconstruction and signing interface. Journey 2 describes the combined memorize-and-sign concept but never reaches the actual signing page; journey 6 fills the memorize form but stops there. This journey clicks the → Go action for 'Reconstruct + sign block', verifies that the destination page renders a meaningful block-signing interface (block reconstruction data, hash, PoL score, signature, or commit controls) rather than a blank or error page, and exercises any signing/commit controls the page exposes. This corresponds to the design doc's chain and block-creation endpoints — the primary blockchain commit action that makes the app fundamentally functional or broken.

existingJourneys.name: Memorize sample text then verify the Graph page displays the built knowledge graph — the IR-learning-to-visualization pipeline
existingJourneys.description: The Graph page (S6) currently shows 'No graph — go to Memorize' because no text has been memorized yet. The complete core workflow is: load sample source text via Charger Wailly (S32) on the Memorize page, click Memorize (S31) to trigger IR learning, then navigate to the Graph page (S6) and verify that a knowledge graph is now displayed — nodes, edges, or a graph visualization — rather than the empty 'No graph' message. This chains the IR-learning submission with graph visualization verification, testing that the memorization output actually produces a persistent, viewable graph — the core Proof-of-Learning data structure that block signing depends on. Journey 6 fills the memorize form and checks for progress on the Memorize page, but never navigates to the Graph page to verify the graph was actually built and is viewable there. A memorize action that claims success but produces no viewable graph is a defect this journey exposes.

existingJourneys.name: Distribute encrypted text chunks across the P2P pool — the E2E ML-KEM-768 post-quantum distributed computation workflow
existingJourneys.description: Navigate to the P2P Network section and exercise the distributed computation pool (E2E ML-KEM-768): fill the 'Texte à distribuer' field (S51) with realistic sample text to be chunked and encrypted, scroll to bottom to reveal any distribute/send controls below the fold, activate them if present, and verify that the pool job status updates (Jobs counter increments, Incoming counter changes, or a distribution/chunking confirmation appears) rather than staying at 0/idle. This covers the core post-quantum encryption feature — ML-KEM-768 chunked encrypted computation distribution across P2P peers — that is the primary differentiator of the ARTCB blockchain and that no existing journey exercises. Journey 9 covers peer addition and synchronization but does not exercise the distributed computation pool's text-input surface (S51), which is the pool's primary data-entry interaction.

existingJourneys.name: Launch mining from the Mining page console — the block-mining script execution path
existingJourneys.description: Navigate to the Mining section (S9) and verify the mining status panel renders meaningfully (PoL score, blocks mined, total rewards, halving countdown). Then click the Mining page's Console button (S38) — labelled 'Launch mining via — real scripts on user machine' — which is a distinct entry point from the debug console navigated to in journeys 10 and 21. Verify the destination renders a meaningful console or script-launch interface rather than a blank page, and if it lands on the CLI console, execute a mining-related command (e.g. 'mine' or 'chain status') and verify the console returns a meaningful response rather than an error or empty output. This tests the mining launch path — the primary blockchain block-creation mechanism — from the Mining section's own Console action, which no existing journey exercises. Journey 1 only navigates to the Mining page and verifies it renders; journeys 10 and 21 exercise the debug console via the SYSTEM nav, not via the Mining page's launch action.

existingJourneys.name: View a mined block's full details from the Chain page — the blockchain block inspection workflow
existingJourneys.description: Now that a block has been mined (Bloc #0 visible on the dashboard and Chain page), navigate to the Chain section, click on the mined block in the block list to open its detail view, verify that the detail view shows meaningful blockchain data (block hash, PoL score, reward, visibility, graph_id, or transaction details) rather than a blank or error page, then navigate back to the chain list. This tests the core block-inspection functionality — the ability to drill into a specific block and examine its on-chain contents — which is fundamental to a blockchain dashboard and that no existing journey exercises. Journey 1 only verifies the Chain page renders with a block table; this journey exercises the block-detail drill-down that is the primary interactive feature of a chain explorer.

existingJourneys.name: View F3 System debug metrics and dashboard demo-live logs — the blockchain node infrastructure monitoring workflow
existingJourneys.description: Navigate to the F3System debug page (S10) — a core SYSTEM-section surface no journey has visited — and verify the system debug screen renders meaningful node infrastructure metrics: CPU core count and load, RAM usage, disk usage, network throughput, GPU/FAISS status, and optimization parameters. Scroll to bottom to reveal any below-the-fold system details. Then navigate back to the dashboard and click the 'Logs' link (S23) in the Last demo_live section — a distinct entry point from the SYSTEM nav Logs tab (S11) covered by journey 3 — and verify the destination shows meaningful demo-live log entries with timestamps and step markers. This chains two infrastructure monitoring surfaces into a complete node-health inspection workflow, corresponding to the design doc's /api/v1/node/status and /api/v1/dashboard/logs/demo-live endpoints that no existing journey exercises through these entry points.

existingJourneys.name: Select a wallet from the wallet list and verify its details — the wallet inspection and active-wallet verification workflow
existingJourneys.description: Navigate to the Wallets page, click on an existing wallet entry in the wallet list (S37) to view or select it, and verify that the wallet detail view shows meaningful information — wallet name, balance, full address, transaction history, or wallet configuration — rather than a blank or error page. Then verify the wallet becomes the active/selected wallet (reflected in the header or wallet selector) and navigate to another section such as Governance or Mining to confirm the active wallet is reflected in that context. This is a core wallet management workflow — the ability to inspect and activate an existing wallet from the list — that no existing journey exercises. Journeys 4 and 15 cover wallet creation and connection by address, but neither clicks on a wallet in the list to inspect its details and verify it becomes the active wallet across the dashboard.

existingJourneys.name: Search a blockchain node via the Quick Start action — the graph node lookup workflow
existingJourneys.description: The dashboard's Quick Start section lists 'Search a node' with a → Go action (S21) — one of the four primary entry points the dashboard presents to users. No existing journey exercises this action or the node-search interface it leads to. Journey 24 covers the 'Explore the graph' action and journey 16 covers AI Memory memo search, but the 'Search a node' Quick Start path — which searches for specific nodes within the blockchain's knowledge graph — is completely untested. This journey clicks the → Go action for 'Search a node', verifies that the destination page renders a meaningful node-search interface (a search input, query form, or node-list view) rather than a blank or error page, exercises any search field it exposes by entering a plausible node query, and verifies that the search produces meaningful output (a list of matching nodes, a graph highlight, or an empty-result message) rather than nothing happening. This corresponds to the core blockchain graph-query functionality that the design doc's chain and graph endpoints support.

existingJourneys.description: Exercise the app's primary blockchain UI by navigating from the dashboard through the three core CHAIN-section tabs — Chain, Wallets, and Mining — verifying that each section switch produces meaningful blockchain-related content (block list, wallet list, mining status) rather than a blank or broken page. This corresponds to the design doc's requirement that the dashboard at / shows the blockchain UI and that chain, wallet, and mining endpoints are exercised.

existingJourneys.name: Query blockchain API endpoints through the debug console — health, chain status, and node status verification
existingJourneys.description: Journey 10 only types 'help' in the console. This journey exercises the console more deeply by running actual API-query commands that correspond to the design doc's REST endpoints: type 'health' and execute to verify a JSON health-status response (HTTP 200 equivalent, correct field names), then type 'chain status' and execute to verify a JSON chain-status response with block height and verification fields. This directly fulfills the design doc's requirement to 'test all REST endpoints, verify JSON responses, HTTP 200, correct field names, no errors' through the dashboard's terminal-equivalent UI — a distinct behaviour from merely confirming the console returns a help listing.

existingJourneys.name: View Governance PoL scores, API Keys, and AI Memory — blockchain governance and access management sections
existingJourneys.description: Navigate from the dashboard through three untouched CORE/SYSTEM sections — Governance (S15, corresponding to /api/v1/pol/score Proof-of-Learn scoring), API Keys (S17, for blockchain API access management), and AI Memory (S18) — verifying that each section switch renders meaningful governance/access/memory content rather than a blank or broken page. These are core ARTCB dashboard surfaces that no existing journey exercises.

existingJourneys.name: Create a new wallet and verify it appears in the wallet list — the blockchain wallet generation flow
existingJourneys.description: Navigate to the Wallets section and exercise the wallet creation form — fill the wallet name field and click Generate — then verify the new wallet appears in the wallet list and can be selected. This covers the design doc's /api/v1/wallet/create and /api/v1/wallet/list functionality, a core blockchain surface no existing journey exercises. The wallet creation form fields (S33 name input and S34 Generate button) are the primary wallet management workflow of the ARTCB dashboard.

existingJourneys.name: Fill the Memorize IR-learning form end-to-end — session, LLM toggle, distributed calc toggle, source text, and submit
existingJourneys.description: Navigate to the Memorize page and fully exercise the IR-learning data-entry form: fill the session_id field, toggle the use_llm checkbox, toggle the distributed calculation (pool E2E) checkbox, load a sample source via the Charger Wailly button (or type source text), then click Memorize to submit. Verify that the form submits and the Proof-of-Learning / graph-building panel shows progress or a result rather than staying idle. This covers the design doc's /api/v1/ir/learn endpoint — the core IR learning workflow — with every form field exercised, which no existing journey does (journey 2 only describes the combined quick-start navigation, not the full form). The form fields (S26 session, S27 use_llm, S28 distributed calc, S30 source text, S31 Memorize, S32 Charger Wailly) are all now visible and testable.

existingJourneys.name: Configure an AI provider integration end-to-end — select provider, fill name, model, and API key, then connect
existingJourneys.description: Navigate to the Integrations section (S13) and fully exercise the AI provider configuration form: select a provider from the dropdown (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, or OpenRouter), fill the integration name field, fill the model field, fill the API key field, then click Connect. Verify that the form submits and produces a connection confirmation or status change rather than staying idle. This covers the ARTCB dashboard's AI integration configuration — a core surface that feeds the IR-learning and Proof-of-Learning workflows — with every form field exercised. No existing journey covers the Integrations page or its configuration form (S41–S45).

existingJourneys.name: Create a blockchain group and join it — the group formation and wallet-binding workflow
existingJourneys.description: Navigate to the Groups section (S16) and fully exercise the group creation form: fill the group name field, fill any configuration fields (version, etc.), select an active wallet, click Create, then click Join to join the group. Verify that the group is created and that joining produces a confirmation or membership status change. This covers the ARTCB dashboard's group governance workflow — a core blockchain community/consensus surface with a multi-field form (S53–S60) that no existing journey exercises. It corresponds to the design doc's requirement that all blockchain core surfaces be tested.

existingJourneys.name: Add a P2P network peer and synchronize all peers — blockchain network management workflow
existingJourneys.description: Navigate to the P2P Network section (S14) and exercise the peer management workflow: fill the peer connection detail fields (S47, S48, S49 — fields with no visible label or placeholder identifying them, so the user cannot tell what each box expects), click Ajouter (S50) to add the peer, then click Synchroniser tous les pairs (S46) to sync the full peer list. Verify that adding a peer produces feedback (a confirmation or the peer appearing in the list) and that synchronization produces a status update or confirmation. This exercises the design doc's /api/v1/p2p/peers endpoint functionality beyond mere viewing — the core blockchain networking peer-addition and sync workflow that no existing journey covers (journey 3 only navigates to P2P/Logs/Console without exercising the peer form).

existingJourneys.name: Generate an API key end-to-end — fill the key name, set expiry, and generate — verifying the key is created with a confirmation
Fill the AI Memory form and create a memory entry — the AI contributor registration workflow
existingJourneys.description: Navigate to the AI Memory section (S18) and fully exercise the AI memory creation form: fill the contributor/agent name field (S61, placeholder 'Cursor dev, ChatGPT bot, LangChain…') and activate the submit control (S62). Verify that the form submits and produces a confirmation or that the new memory entry appears in the list rather than staying idle. Journey 5 only navigates to the AI Memory page without exercising its form — this journey covers the data-entry form the AI Memory page exposes, satisfying the form-coverage requirement for a page whose primary purpose is to register AI agents/contributors that feed the Proof-of-Learning and IR-learning workflows.

existingJourneys.name: Create a governance proposal — select voting wallet, fill title/description/version, and submit
existingJourneys.description: Navigate to the Governance section and fully exercise the governance proposal creation form: select a voting wallet (S52), fill the title field (S53, which has no visible label or placeholder identifying it, so the user cannot tell what the box expects), fill the description field (S54, also unlabeled/unplaceholdered), fill the version field (S55), then click Créer (S56) to submit the proposal. Verify that the proposal is created and the app gives feedback — a confirmation, the new proposal appearing in the Propositions list, or a status change — rather than nothing happening. This covers the ARTCB dashboard's on-chain governance workflow (1 wallet = 1 vote, community accepts/rejects major updates), a core blockchain consensus surface whose data-entry form no existing journey exercises. Journey 5 only navigates to the Governance page without filling the form; journey 8 covers the Groups page, not Governance proposals. The title and description fields present no visible label or placeholder, so a user cannot recognize what each box expects from the field itself — a recognition defect this journey exposes.

existingJourneys.name: View AI Memory status and memo list, then create a memo and verify it appears — the complete memo lifecycle workflow
existingJourneys.description: Navigate to the AI Memory section and exercise the two untested tabs — Status (S68) and Memos (S69) — then create a memo and verify it appears in the list. First click the Status tab and verify the JSON status panel renders meaningful data (agent_ready, chain height, PoL average, memory count) rather than a blank or error. Then click the Memos tab and verify the memo list renders (either existing engraved memos or an empty-state message). Then click New memo, fill the content textarea (S83), select a memo type (S84), fill the Session ID (S85), and click 'Graver dans la blockchain' (S86) to engrave it. Finally, click the Memos tab (S69) again and verify the newly created memo now appears in the list — confirming the on-chain commit actually persisted and is retrievable, satisfying the data-redisplay requirement. This tests the complete AI Memory read-create-verify lifecycle: the Status and Memos tabs (S68, S69) are the last untested primary surfaces on the AI Memory page, and verifying a freshly engraved memo appears in the Memos list is the critical persistence check that journey 22 does not perform.

existingJourneys.name: Connect an existing wallet by address — the wallet access/login flow
existingJourneys.description: Navigate to the Wallets section and exercise the 'Connexion — J'ai déjà un wallet' form: fill the wallet address field (S35) with the address of the wallet created earlier in the run (or any visible wallet address from the wallet list), click 'Se connecter' (S36), and verify that the connection succeeds — the wallet becomes active/selected and its balance and details are displayed — rather than showing an error or staying idle. This covers the design doc's /api/v1/wallet/list wallet-access functionality: the primary 'connect existing wallet' workflow that is distinct from wallet creation (journey 4 only creates a wallet; this journey tests the login/connect path an existing wallet holder uses to access their account). The form field (S35) has a placeholder 'artcb1… ou adresse Base64 de votre wallet' identifying it, and the submit control (S36) is the primary wallet authentication action.

existingJourneys.name: Add an AI Memory webhook endpoint — fill URL and label, submit, and verify the webhook is registered
existingJourneys.description: Navigate to the AI Memory section, click the Webhooks tab (S73), and fully exercise the webhook creation form that was revealed: fill the webhook URL field (S76, placeholder 'URL HTTPS (https://...)') and the label field (S77, placeholder 'Label'), then click '+ Ajouter' (S78) to submit. Verify that adding the webhook produces feedback — a confirmation message, the new webhook appearing in an active webhooks list, or a status change — rather than nothing happening. Journey 17 navigates to the Webhooks tab and describes viewing webhook management content, but the actual webhook creation form (S76–S78) has never been filled and submitted. This is a data-entry form whose primary purpose is to register an HTTPS endpoint that external AI tools (Cursor, ChatGPT, LangChain) receive live blockchain memory updates at — a core integration surface of the ARTCB AI Memory backend. The form-coverage rule requires exercising it rather than leaving it as a visited-but-unfilled page.

existingJourneys.name: Configure AI Memory webhooks and open a live data stream — the external AI tool real-time integration pipeline
existingJourneys.description: Navigate to the AI Memory section and exercise the real-time integration surfaces no journey has touched: click the Webhooks tab (S73) to view/configure webhook endpoints for external AI tools, then switch to the Stream tab (S74), click 'Ouvrir le stream' (S79) to open a live data stream, and click 'Rafraichir' (S75) to refresh the stream. Verify that the Webhooks tab renders meaningful webhook management content (not a blank page), that opening the stream produces a live data connection or stream output rather than nothing happening, and that refreshing updates the stream. This covers the ARTCB dashboard's real-time AI Memory integration pipeline — the webhook and streaming interfaces that Cursor, ChatGPT, and LangChain use to receive live blockchain memory updates — which is a core external-integration surface that no existing journey exercises. Journey 14 covers memo creation and engraving; journey 16 covers search and export; this journey covers the push/stream side of the AI Memory backend.

existingJourneys.name: Search AI Memory memos and export results — the RAG retrieval and data export workflow
existingJourneys.description: Navigate to the AI Memory section and exercise the memo search and export workflow: click the Search tab (S71), enter search terms in the search field, click Rechercher (S82) to execute the search, and verify that search results appear (a list of matching memos or an empty-result message). Then switch to the Export tab (S72), select an export format from the available options (S80 — Summary/JSONL (RAG)/JSON complet), click Exporter (S81), and verify that export output is produced (a download, a JSON dump, or an on-screen data block). This covers the AI Memory section's retrieval and data-export path — the RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) query interface that external AI tools (Cursor, ChatGPT, LangChain) use to read from the ARTCB blockchain memory backend — which is a distinct behavior from memo creation (journey 14) and exercises the read/query/export side of the /api/v1 agent-memory surface that no existing journey tests.
